_about: PRO batch 48: era 4, The Veteran (34-37), set 3.

scenarios.title: The Last Contract Negotiation Tactics
scenarios.text: Your agent wants to play hardball one last time: hold firm, threaten free agency, make the club pay for your loyalty. It's your last contract year, probably.

choices.label: Let your agent play hardball
choices.result: Hardball, played well. The club pays more than it wanted to, and the general manager is cool with you all spring.

choices.label: Ask for a fair deal
choices.result: A fair deal, asked for directly by you, in the general manager's office. It comes quickly, and nobody has to pretend anything to anyone.

choices.label: Talk to your family first
choices.result: The family, asked what they need from this last contract. Their answer is simpler than your agent's, and you go with it.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Farewell Speech
scenarios.text: A retiring teammate gives a farewell speech in the locker room that leaves the room completely silent: about fear, about his father, about the game that saved him.

choices.label: Be the first to stand
choices.result: The first one on your feet, clapping. The whole room follows you up, and he can't finish wiping his eyes before the applause stops.

choices.label: Find him afterward
choices.result: Afterward, in the parking lot, a long hug and few words. He says he wrote it with your help, years ago, without knowing.

choices.label: Write down what he said
choices.result: His best line, written on the inside of your locker door that night. You read it before every game for the rest of your career.

scenarios.title: The Team Chaplain
scenarios.text: The team chaplain catches you in the hallway after a hard week and asks how you're really doing. He's asked before; this time he waits for the answer.

choices.label: Tell him the truth
choices.result: The truth, in his small office, for an hour: the fear of the end, the hip, the house. You feel lighter walking out.

choices.label: Ask about his life instead
choices.result: His life, asked about, for once. He tells you about his own father, and you end up talking about yours.

choices.label: Say you're fine
choices.result: Fine, you say, and he nods and lets you go. He leaves the door open, and you walk past it twice that month.

scenarios.title: The Old Locker Room Rules
scenarios.text: The young players have changed the locker room rules: new music, new fines, a new rule about phones in meetings. They ask your opinion, a little nervously.

choices.label: Back the new rules
choices.result: The new rules, backed completely, in front of the room. The young players walk taller, and the old rules don't come back.

choices.label: Suggest one change
choices.result: One change, suggested gently: keep the old rule about the rookie dinner. They agree, and the old tradition survives another generation.

choices.label: Let them run it
choices.result: It's their room now, you say, and you mean it. They're surprised and proud, and they still ask your opinion.

scenarios.title: The Media Room Farewell
scenarios.text: A beat reporter who has covered you since your rookie year is retiring. He asks for one last interview, at the diner where you did the first one.

choices.label: Give him the best interview of your career
choices.result: The best interview of your career, at the same booth. He writes it in one night, and it's the story people remember.

choices.label: Turn the tables
choices.result: His career, asked about instead. He talks for an hour about the coaches and players he loved, and you buy his breakfast.

choices.label: Bring {holder}
choices.result: {holder}, brought along to the diner. The three of you laugh about the old stories, and the reporter forgets to write anything down.

scenarios.title: The Trainer's Retirement
scenarios.text: The trainer who has taped your ankle every game day since you arrived is retiring. He says your ankle is the one he'll miss, which you choose to take as a compliment.

choices.label: Give him a send-off
choices.result: A send-off in the training room, with every player he ever taped. You tape his ankle, badly, and he laughs until he cries.

choices.label: Learn to tape it yourself
choices.result: His last lesson: how to tape your own ankle properly. You practice for a week, and his successor is impressed.

choices.label: Write him a note
choices.result: A note, left in his kit bag, about every game day morning. He reads it at his retirement party and has to stop.

scenarios.title: New Gear, Old Habits
scenarios.text: New cleats, new balls, new tracking technology: the league has changed the equipment, and your old routine, built over fifteen years, doesn't fit any of it.

choices.label: Rebuild the routine
choices.result: The routine, rebuilt over a month with the equipment staff. It's humbling, and the new version is better than the old one.

choices.label: Ask the young kickers
choices.result: The young kickers, asked how they're adjusting to the new gear. They teach you three tricks, and you all laugh about it at lunch.

choices.label: Keep what you can
choices.result: Everything you can keep, kept: the old warmup, the old count. You adapt the rest slowly, and it works well enough.

scenarios.title: The Young Kicker's Thank-You
scenarios.text: A young kicker at another club thanks you publicly for advice that saved his career, advice you don't remember giving. He describes the conversation in detail.

choices.label: Call him back
choices.result: Your call reaches him that evening, and the old conversation comes back to you halfway through. He cries; you pretend you're not.

choices.label: Thank him back publicly
choices.result: A public thank-you, back to him, on the record. It becomes a story about passing things on, which it is.

choices.label: Keep giving advice
choices.result: More advice, more often, to every young kicker who asks you anything. You never know which conversation will matter years later.

scenarios.title: The Ring of Honor Nomination
scenarios.text: You're nominated for the club's ring of honor while you're still playing. The vote is in the spring, and the fans have started a campaign with your face on a T-shirt.

choices.label: Buy a T-shirt
choices.result: A T-shirt, bought and worn proudly to practice. The fans love it, and the specialists buy matching ones the next day.

choices.label: Stay out of the campaign
choices.result: Out of it entirely, on purpose. The vote happens without you, and either way, you'll have finished your career right here.

choices.label: Thank the fans properly
choices.result: A proper thank-you, at a fan event, signing for three hours. Whatever happens in the vote, they know what they meant.

scenarios.title: The Last Opening Day
scenarios.text: What might be your last opening day, and you notice everything: the smell of the grass, the anthem, the way the snapper always touches the ball twice.

choices.label: Notice everything on purpose
choices.result: Every detail, noticed on purpose, all day. You'll remember it forever, and you kick better than you have in weeks.

choices.label: Treat it like any other day
choices.result: Any other day, on purpose, from breakfast to the last kick. The routine is the routine, and the nostalgia can wait patiently until December.

choices.label: Bring the family onto the field
choices.result: The family, brought onto the field before warmups. The kids stand right on the logo, and {love_interest} takes the photo that ends up framed.
